transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled 15:00–15:52)
Attendees: Sophie Ramirez (Redwood AE), Michael Chen (Redwood SE), Mark O'Neill (BlueHarbor CTO), Jenna Park (Head of Legal), Tom Reyes (Procurement), Laila Singh (Cloud Ops)

Summary:
Quick procurement and legal triage focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA credit mechanics, egress and data residency concerns, and pricing model for a pilot. Customer has Fed-sensitive clients and wants on-prem pattern/options, KMS integration, and a clear path for escrow/exit. Agreed next steps and owners (see action items).

Topics:
- MSA exceptions and DPA specificities (data residency, processing scope)
- SLA definition, uptime measurement and credit calculation
- Pricing: committed capacity vs consumption, egress fees, bulk discounts
- Security: KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, SOC 2 and audit logs retention
- Pilot scope and success criteria (latency, token costs, accuracy)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie (AE): All right everyone good to go. Thanks for joining, this is Sophie Ramirez from Redwood Inference, I have Michael from Solutions Engineering with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:04] Mark (CTO): Hi Sophie, doing well, thanks. We have Jenna from legal and Tom from procurement, and Laila from cloud ops on the line.
[00:09] Jenna (Legal): Hi all. I'll try not to slow things down but want to make sure we capture the DPA notes.
[00:13] Sophie: Perfect. The agenda we circulated was MSA/DPA redlines, SLA mechanics, pricing and egress, and then pilot timelines — is that accurate?
[00:18] Tom (Procurement): Yes that's right. Procurement wants to understand payment terms and PO language now to avoid later hold-ups.
[00:22] Michael (SE): I'll jump in on the technical bits — we'll cover the private deployment and KMS options you asked about in the doc.

[00:45] Sophie: Jenna, do you want to start with the DPA expectations? We got your preliminary redlines last week.
[00:49] Jenna: Sure. High level: data residency for EU customers is non-negotiable for us. We also want a clause that explicitly says Redwood won't use customer data to train models. We saw the general statement but want it stronger and auditable. Also retention windows: 90 days for logs, but we may want certain PD logs deleted sooner.
[01:05] Michael: Understood. Technically we can support per-tenant KV cache purge and shorter log retention in Private deployments; for Hosted we have configurable retention and can discuss dedicated pools for isolation.
[01:13] Laila: For Fed-sensitive workloads we need KMS integration, ideally customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS). Also HSM backed keys for long-term storage.
[01:22] Michael: We offer KMS integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and an HSM option for Private. There's a config knob so that only ciphertext leaves your VPC, and we can document the flow.

[01:40] Tom: On the MSA side, procurement flagged an escrow/exit clause — if Redwood discontinues a model we need a pathway to extract caches and a way to validate model continuity. What do you recommend?
[01:49] Sophie: We can add a tiered transition commitment: for Dedicated/Private contracts we commit to a 90-day data export window and provide export tooling; escrow for model binaries is possible on enterprise plans. We typically avoid escrow for hosted open models but we can negotiate.
[02:04] Jenna: We also want SLA credits defined relative to 1-second vs 5-second p95 latencies across the route — can you give us language?
[02:12] Michael: SLA credits are usually uptime based, e.g., monthly availability below 99.9% nets a credit formula. Per-latency SLOs are trickier due to workload variance but we can define a latency-tiered SLO for Dedicated pools, and provide transparent token-by-token telemetry to audit.

[02:35] Sophie: To be explicit, for Dedicated we'll provide a 99.95% availability SLA with target p95 latency under the agreed profile; for Hosted we'll offer 99.9% availability. Credits: standard is service credit percentage of monthly fees; we can pass you draft language.
[02:47] Tom: We need to know the measurement window and the exception carve-outs (eg, force majeure, customer misconfiguration). Please add examples.
[02:55] Michael: We'll include a measurement spec: chosen endpoints, measurement agents, error classes that count as downtime. We'll include normal exceptions.

[03:12] Mark: Pricing: your hosted per-token rates are competitive but egress fees are a big unknown. Our cloud contracts are sensitive to egress for inference outputs. Do you charge egress separately for hosted? And how does that work for Dedicated?
[03:23] Sophie: Good question. For Hosted we currently incorporate output egress into the per-token price for most regions, but for very high-volume customers we sometimes separate egress as a line item. For Dedicated you typically pay for infra egress according to the cloud provider plus our managed data transfer fee; we can model both approaches.
[03:37] Tom: Can you provide an example bill for 5M tokens/day and 50TB egress a month?
[03:42] Michael: Yes — we'll produce a sample billing spreadsheet with committed capacity and burst buffers showing per-token, compute, and egress line items, including sustained-use discounts for multi-month commits.

[03:58] Jenna: Another legal note: audit logs retention — we need for up to 7 years for certain regulated clients. Is that supported and at what cost?
[04:07] Michael: Long-term log retention is supported as an add-on to the observability store. We'll give options: short-term hot logs for 90 days included, archive to S3-ish for multi-year at a per-GB monthly rate.
[04:18] Laila: For on-prem deployments, what's the upgrade path? We can't be offline for a major upgrade.
[04:24] Michael: For Private we support rolling upgrades with blue/green deploys and can run a staged canary in your environment. We'll coordinate maintenance windows and have a rollback snapshot policy.

[04:40] Sophie: Let's cover the DPA clause about training. Jenna you said you want a stronger non-training clause — what language would you consider acceptable?
[04:47] Jenna: Something like 'Customer Data will not be used by Redwood, directly or indirectly, to improve or modify any model offered by Redwood or any third party without explicit written consent.' That's the kind of hard language we prefer.
[04:59] Michael: Technically we can commit to that for Data processed under Private and Dedicated with certain telemetry exceptions; for Hosted we can offer a contractual promise and isolate telemetry for evaluation with opt-out.

[05:20] Tom: Procurement wants to align on payment terms: Net 60 is our default, but Redwood's billing cadence is monthly upfront. Any flexibility?
[05:27] Sophie: We can do monthly invoices with Net 30 on enterprise contracts; Net 60 is challenging but could be agreed on with a slight fee or with an escrow/advance arrangement. We'll note that as negotiable.

[05:40] Mark: One more thing — export controls. Any models or deployments that might be restricted for certain geos?
[05:46] Michael: Models are generally open-source family; we don't include restricted-territory models by default. But we can add contractual territory limitations and block certain cloud regions from being used for customer's data.

[05:58] Sophie: This is great — sounds like alignment on the main points. Let's talk about the pilot. What success criteria do you need?
[06:03] Mark: For pilot: 1) sub-600ms p95 on our short prompts, 2) cost under $X per 1k tokens (we'll provide target), 3) stability during 8–6 business hours for two weeks. Also we want a data flow diagram for compliance review.
[06:16] Michael: We'll propose a 2-week pilot on a Dedicated small pool or on-hosted plus a dedicated fallback; we'll produce the perf plan and a runbook for the pilot. We'll also prepare the flow diagram.

[06:28] Jenna: We'll circulate a list of DPA exceptions we'd like and any regulatory articles; will Redwood accept limited redlines rather than full DPA rewrite?
[06:36] Sophie: Yes, we typically accept targeted redlines. Send the highlighted sections and we'll respond inline.

[06:45] Tom: On procurement gating: our legal needs the MSA clean, procurement needs approved PO language, and finance needs a forecast for 12 months. We'll need those docs to progress.
[06:54] Sophie: Understood — we'll send the pricing projection and the standard PO language. Also, we'll include an option for PO with milestone payments if that helps.

[07:05] Laila: Small ops question — is there RBAC for token-level access? We want to limit dev/test keys from seeing production traffic.
[07:12] Michael: Yes, Redwood Console supports token scoping and per-team RBAC. We can give you role templates and an example RBAC policy.

[07:30] Sophie: Ok let's recap next steps: I'll send MSA/DPA redlines, pricing spreadsheet, and PO templates; Michael will run the technical deep-dive and prepare the sample billing and perf plan; Jenna will send prioritized DPA exceptions; Tom will confirm procurement timeline. Anything to add?
[07:46] Mark: Could you also include a short note on SLA measurement spec so we can review with our SREs?
[07:52] Michael: Absolutely, we'll include the measurement spec and the tracing hooks you can pull into your observability.

[08:05] Jenna: One procedural Q — for KMS keys we need an attestation that keys never leave HSM. Is there a standard attestation you can provide?
[08:13] Michael: We have a standard KMS integration diagram and an attestation template we can sign on the enterprise contract; we'll attach that.

[08:30] Sophie: Great, we'll get these artifacts out this week. Any final items?
[08:34] Tom: No, thanks. We'll look for the docs and target an internal procurement review next Tuesday.
[08:38] Sophie: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the technical deep-dive and a copy of the MSA redlines.

End of transcript
